text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- Electricity consumer prices may rise if oil group Neste and power company IVO merge, says Central Organization of Finnish Trade Unions (SAK) official.
- The Financial Supervision Authority (RATA) must give its blessing to combination shopping and banking cards many Finnish retailers are planning with banks, government lawyer says.
- Restrictions on travellers importing alcohol to Finland to be reviewed by the European Commission. @
- Driving manners reveal drivers' personal characteristics, a doctoral dissertation shows.
- Crown Prince of Thailand paid official visit to Finland on Thursday.
- Markka is facing pressures to appreciate, at least in the short run, Finnish analysts say.
- Core of Finnish ownership in telecoms company Nokia is melting after main Finnish investors sell their shares. @

- A merger between Neste and Ivo could harm competition; but its advantages are worth studying, says Tauno Matomaki, head of energy political committee at the Confederation of Finnish Industry and Employers (TT).
- Government clearly behind in bid to halve unemployment.
- A history of Nokia since 1966 is being prepared, Finnish historian Martti Haikia says. @

- Many MPs do not have the courage to make decisions on European economic and monetary union (EMU) betraying their constituencies by demanding a conferendum, Finance Minister says in a interview in Nykypaiva magazine.
- Finns will start coordinating European ozone layer research at a centre based in Helsinki next year.
- Finland still leads criminal homicide statistics in Nordic and Western Europe; economic growth has increased alcohol consumption and crimes, study shows.
